edgeBE.pinned_note: PINNED 2026-08-30, not produced by HAT_groin_joint_fit.py's ranking. The ranking's own answer (edgeBE M=160 f=0.8, zeroBE M=140 f=1.0) is archived at archive/joint_fit_RAILED_ranking_20260830.json. It railed because it scores BOTH periods jointly, and period 2 records a fillet RELEASE the module cannot produce at any (M, f) -- fitting it is the wrong thing to attempt (see hard-structures/groin/GROIN_PLAN.md). M = 60 comes from the period-1 D4-D8 demeaned fit at be1 = -42.6 and is reproduced by the independent D3-D9 window; f = 0.6 comes from the 1967-2018 rig, where it is bracketed on both sides. Both presets carry the same pair deliberately: a zeroBE groin fit is meaningless (with no edge forcing the groin absorbs the missing source/sink term and improves monotonically to the grid edge), so zeroBE inherits the edgeBE decision rather than a fit of its own. RE-RUNNING STAGE 5 WILL OVERWRITE THIS FILE with the railed ranking -- re-pin afterwards.

calibBE.pinned_note: PINNED 2026-08-31, INHERITED from edgeBE rather than fitted. calibBE is DERIVED FROM the edgeBE groin fit: HAT_be_zone_LOESS_analysis.py with GROIN_AWARE_BASE_RUN=True builds the source/sink field from a base run already carrying M=60/f=0.6, so the field is what the groin could NOT explain. Re-fitting a groin against that field would be circular -- it would be fitting to a residual constructed by removing this exact groin. M was fitted against edgeBE precisely because edgeBE imposes nothing at D5/D6. Without this entry HAT_run_all.py stage 6 prints 'skipping its groin runs' and calibBE gets no groin arm at all.
